Disney lost his hit character. The one thing he kept built something bigger.

Kevin Trudeau tells how Walt Disney's partners used a contract trick to take his cartoon character. Disney spent a long time trying to get it back.

Then he accepted that they had taken the character, not his ability to create. He sat down and created Mickey Mouse. Almost nobody remembers Oswald the Rabbit today.

What skill of yours could you rebuild from, even after a loss?

#ad #success #mindset #kevintrudeau

The strongest drive may not be the dream. It may be what you refuse to live with.

Kevin Trudeau says the first step most books skip is to name what you are no longer willing to accept. He points to champions like Tiger Woods and Roger Federer, who say they love winning but hate losing even more.

His point: people will do more to avoid pain than to gain pleasure, so know what you will not tolerate.

What is the one thing you are finished tolerating?

#ad #mindset #goals #kevintrudeau

Kevin's way to stop fearing a wrong decision: win or learn.

Kevin Trudeau says he doesn't worry about choosing wrong, because every choice either wins or teaches him something. That makes each one perfect in his eyes.

He also says people treat every opportunity as the only one. In his view it is one opportunity in a lifetime, and a thousand more are coming down the road.

What opportunity are you still beating yourself up for missing?

#ad #mindset #confidence #kevintrudeau

Hiring more people may be what keeps your business stuck.

Kevin Trudeau describes a business owner whose sales stayed flat while profits kept falling, because he kept adding overhead. Kevin told him he was trying to push a rope.

Kevin then shares the view of his friend Chainsaw Al Dunlap, a turnaround expert: cut expenses everywhere, because profits are the money that stays in your pocket.

Where in your business are you adding more instead of cutting?
